name: Prize crossword No 26,657
preamble: Eight solutions (one of them fictional) have something in common, not further defined.

clue.text: Restrain mongrel starting to bark

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
opening letter of the word bark

explanation.surface: A dog owner holds back a mutt that has begun barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restrain' sits naturally beside the dog, but it is the definition; the mongrel and its bark supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb something is to check or keep it under control, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Team is up to making two appearances in London

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a side is a team
the letter pair that occurs twice in the word London

explanation.surface: A team is in a position to appear twice in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison, the inventor, is one of the eight Thomases the preamble leaves undefined. 'Making two appearances in London' is a cryptic pointer to the letters seen twice in that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph.

clue.text: Fault finder cites Right Reverend's unruly gathering here in Paris

indicators.note: unruly things refuse to stay in order, so these letters are rearranged
to gather something is to take it in, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for the title of a bishop
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A carping critic quotes a bishop's rowdy meeting held in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' looks like a noun for the bishop's meeting, but it is a verb telling the rearranged letters to enclose the French word; 'here in Paris' is a common way to ask for a French translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A criticiser is someone who finds fault, so the phrase describes the person exactly.

clue.text: Yellows all at sea after losing centre

indicators.note: losing the centre means dropping the middle letter of the word
something all at sea is confused and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; its middle letter, the fourth of seven, is L

explanation.surface: Yellow-coloured boats are drifting aimlessly at sea, missing their middle section.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Wolsey was Henry VIII's cardinal and chancellor. Drop the central L of YELLOWS, then rearrange the six remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Cardinal Thomas Wolsey was Henry VIII's chief minister.

clue.text: Old car rallying point

blocks.note: first meaning: a car made by the defunct British ... Motor Company
second meaning: a flag around which troops gather in battle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a vintage car rally; the Standard was a British make of car, and a standard is a battle flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard was a British car brand, and a standard is also a banner raised for soldiers to rally around.

clue.text: Spirit said to be made from pears

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: perry is an alcoholic drink fermented from pears, like cider from apples

explanation.surface: Someone claims a particular liquor is distilled from pears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a drink, which fits the pears; it is in fact a supernatural being. Perry is a British pear cider.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or elf-like spirit in Persian mythology, a word mostly met in crosswords.

clue.text: Like 5, reported to be angry and oversuspicious

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word is wanted for its sound

blocks.note: 5 down is STANDARD, and par is the standard level
annoyed means angry

explanation.surface: Someone, like the person in another clue, is said to be cross and distrustful.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to STANDARD, which PAR means; the second half is spelt to sound like ANNOYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being paranoid means harbouring excessive, unfounded distrust of others, which is what being oversuspicious describes.

clue.text: Mount where 24 across is one of 4 losing speed

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so those letters drop out

blocks.clueFragment: Mount where 24 across is one of 4
blocks.note: Mount Rushmore carves four presidents, Jefferson among them
to rush is to speed

explanation.surface: A puzzle cross-reference: the mountain where a president is one of four faces.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas More was Henry VIII's chancellor and author of Utopia. Mount Rushmore in South Dakota carries the faces of four US presidents, including Jefferson at 24 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia and was executed by Henry VIII.

clue.text: Dance tour abroad put on first of all

definitions.note: describes the layer of paint applied first, so stands for the noun

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance company's overseas tour is staged before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' reads as overseas travel for the tour, but it signals scrambling. The definition describes paint rather than a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An undercoat is the layer of paint applied before the top coat, so it goes on first.

clue.text: Retroaction regularly is seen amongst the Gods

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a figure of Greek myth

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A backward-acting effect is regularly observed among the deities.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry, one of the nine daughters of Zeus, so she belongs among the gods of Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is a Muse, a minor goddess of Greek mythology, so she is found among the divine company.

clue.text: Stupefy with gamble taken over shipping order

indicators.note: something taken over is covered from above, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a bet is a gamble
SO is the abbreviation for a shipping order

explanation.surface: A risky wager placed on a cargo consignment leaves someone dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken over' sounds like the cargo being seized, but it means the gamble sits over, and so around, the shipping order.
explanation.definitionFit: To besot is to muddle or dull someone's wits, typically with drink or infatuation, a synonym of stupefy.

clue.text: Acting considerately, chucking up role in consortium

indicators.note: to chuck up something is to give it up or abandon it, so those letters are removed
acting means performing a part, so the letters play new roles in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thoughtful member gives up a position within a business group.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R, O, L and E from CONSIDERATELY, then rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of companies or people pooling resources for a shared venture, which is what a consortium is.

clue.text: Frightened as the result of a slight cut in earnings

indicators.note: one thing being inside another means it is enclosed

blocks.note: pay is what one earns
a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: A worker is scared after a small reduction in wages.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cut in earnings' reads as a pay cut, but the cut is a small notch placed inside the pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicky means overcome by sudden fear or anxiety, so it is a close synonym of frightened.

clue.text: Old man at home finds sweetheart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to be in is to be at home
the central letter of the five-letter word sweet, read off its heart

explanation.surface: An elderly man staying in discovers a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Paine wrote Common Sense and Rights of Man. 'Sweetheart' looks like one word for a lover but splits into the word and its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Thomas Paine was the radical pamphleteer of the American Revolution.

clue.text: Against old order once found in Turkey

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a place

blocks.note: anti means opposed to
O is the abbreviation for old
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone opposes an outdated system once seen in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Companions of Honour is a British honour abbreviated CH. Antioch was an ancient city whose site is now Antakya in southern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a great ancient city whose ruins lie at modern Antakya, within present-day Turkey's borders.

clue.text: Beat knowledge and spirit with late finisher

indicators.note: a finisher is what comes at the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to tan someone is to beat them
ken means range of knowledge
gin is a spirit
the closing letter of the word late

explanation.surface: Sharp wits and drink beat someone who finishes late.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas the Tank Engine, the children's railway engine, is the fictional member of the preamble's eight. To tan someone's hide is to thrash them.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Thomas the Tank Engine is the fictional locomotive of children's stories.

clue.text: Only just failing to secure the Labour leadership

indicators.note: failing to hold on to something means it is lost, so that letter drops out
the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: hardly means barely, only just
the opening letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A political candidate narrowly misses winning the leadership of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles. Labour is Britain's main left-of-centre party, which makes the surface sound political.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Thomas Hardy was the novelist and poet of Wessex.

clue.text: Try to get out of manufacturing, which originates in Tibet

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a river

indicators.note: getting out of something means leaving it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: industry is the business of manufacturing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to leave manufacturing, a business that started in Tibet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which' seems to refer to manufacturing, but it is the answer itself: the river Indus rises on the Tibetan plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river of South Asia whose source lies in western Tibet before it flows through Pakistan.

clue.text: Dope can act as stooge for slow administration

blocks.note: a drip is a feeble, dull person, a dope
a feed is a comedian's straight man who sets up the jokes

explanation.surface: An idiot can serve as a fall guy for a sluggish government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Administration' suggests government, but here it means giving medicine. A feed in comedy is the stooge who supplies the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip feed delivers fluid or medicine into a patient gradually, drop by drop, which is giving something slowly.

clue.text: Bar starts with roll of drums

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters of each word

blocks.note: opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A pub's evening begins with a drum roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub or music bar, which suits the drums, but it means a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a thin straight bar of metal or wood, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Consider once more dimwits having a role in limited research

indicators.note: something limited is cut short, so the word is truncated
playing a part inside something places one piece within another

blocks.note: the word cut down to its first three letters, a common abbreviation
asses are fools

explanation.surface: Think again about fools getting a part in a small study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited research' suggests a small study, but it means the word research cut short to its standard abbreviation, with the fools then placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate or judge something again, so it means thinking it over another time.

clue.text: Drain away from lowest point

indicators.note: away suggests letters gone astray from their places, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Water drains off from the lowest spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain away' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, and 'away' rearranges the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom or worst moment of something, literally the point directly beneath an observer.

clue.text: Corrupt secretariat cast out of country

indicators.note: taken out means removed, so those letters go
to corrupt something is to spoil its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crooked government office is expelled from a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' reads as expelled, but cast is letters to remove and only 'out' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast, so it is an example.

clue.text: Quite recently acting in an amorous manner

blocks.note: first meaning: newly, just now
second meaning: in a forward, overfamiliar way, as when someone gets fresh

explanation.walkthrough: To get fresh with someone is to make cheeky romantic or sexual advances, so the adverb serves both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshly means newly or just now, and fresh also describes impudent romantic forwardness.

clue.text: The very best clothes are about to leave processing plant

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters go

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a refinery processes raw materials such as oil or sugar

explanation.surface: The best garments are about to leave a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to leave' reads as soon departing; split it, and 'about' is the letters taken from the front of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Finery is elaborate, showy dress worn on special occasions, someone's best outfit.

clue.text: Limps along having no use of left leg

indicators.note: being without the use of something means it is missing, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to hobble is to walk awkwardly, to limp
L for left; the leg only completes the limping picture

explanation.surface: Someone limps along, unable to use their left leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hobbes was the philosopher who wrote Leviathan.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Thomas Hobbes was the English political philosopher behind Leviathan.

clue.text: Scoffs very loudly — interjecting four times in constitutional convention

indicators.note: to interject is to put something in between, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to jeer is to scoff
fortissimo, the musical direction for very loud
the letter pair that occurs four times in those two words

explanation.surface: Delegates heckle noisily, interrupting four times at a gathering to draft a constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Jefferson drafted the Declaration of Independence. Count the letter pair in cONstitutiONal cONventiON to see the four appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared theme is the forename Thomas, and Thomas Jefferson was the third US president.

clue.text: Root receives Kent cap (just kidding)!

definitions.note: a phrase signalling something not meant seriously; the answer is the noun

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece is put inside another
a cap sits on top, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Joe Root is an England cricket captain and batsman
the opening letter of Kent

explanation.surface: England batsman Joe Root is awarded a county cap by Kent, only in jest.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root plays cricket for Yorkshire and England; Kent is another English county side, and a cap is the honour of selection. 'Root' looks like a plant's root, but it is his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke is something said or done in fun, not meant seriously, which is what 'just kidding' declares.

clue.text: She led church movement in a circle

blocks.note: first meaning: Mary Baker ..., founder of the Christian Science church
second meaning: a swirl of water or air turning round

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a woman leading a congregation in a circular procession; the founder of Christian Science and a swirling current share one surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Baker Eddy founded the Church of Christ, Scientist, and an eddy is a circular current of water or air.

clue.text: George is fit to be called the King

definitions.note: describes a person by nickname, standing for a name

blocks.note: G stands for George, as in the old phonetic alphabet and GR for George Rex
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A man named George is worthy of being crowned monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: With six King Georges in British history, the surface sounds royal; the answer is Clark Gable, whom Hollywood dubbed the King.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable, star of Gone with the Wind, was popularly nicknamed the King of Hollywood.

clue.text: Consumes a variety of teas

indicators.note: a variety offers a different form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drinks many different kinds of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A variety of teas' sounds like a tea sampler, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to take it in and use it up, which matches the verb consumes.

clue.text: Articulated demand to work making bread

indicators.note: articulated means spoken clearly, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a need is a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: A clearly stated demand to get on with baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' suggests a lorry or joints, but here it means spoken; the silent K turns the sound into the baker's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work dough with the hands, pressing and folding it, when making bread.

clue.text: Strict way to call hospital department

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ring is to telephone, to call
ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Tight rules govern how to phone a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are rigorous and exacting, so the word is a close synonym of strict.
